## Professional Summary

Madu Chinemerem Clarence is a Software Engineer specializing in Machine Learning,
with a niche in Deep Learning. He builds end-to-end ML systems — from raw data
ingestion and model training to production deployment and MLOps infrastructure.

He works across the full ML stack: data pipelines, model architecture, training,
evaluation, inference optimization, and cloud deployment. Every architectural
decision is justified by problem constraints — dataset size, latency budget,
compute cost, and interpretability requirements.

He is available for full-time roles, contract engagements, and research
collaborations worldwide.

## Projects

### Météo-Agri CI
Description: Real-time agricultural weather intelligence platform for Côte d'Ivoire.
Ingests live meteorological API data, computes crop-specific risk scores, and
surfaces actionable regional forecasts.
Dataset: Live feeds from OpenWeatherMap API — 7 agro-climatic zones, 72-hour rolling window.
Architecture: Rule-based threshold classifier on normalized meteorological features.
Chosen for interpretability and low inference latency in production.
Stack: Python, Streamlit, OpenWeatherMap API, AWS, GitHub Actions CI/CD
Status: Deployed and live

### WaveShare
Description: Open-source async P2P file transfer library. Solves dependency-free
device-to-device transfer without a cloud relay.
Dataset: Benchmarked across file sizes 1KB–2GB on constrained edge hardware.
Architecture: Async BLE scanner (bleak) + direct TCP socket stream. BLE chosen over
mDNS for battery-constrained devices. SHA-256 for integrity over TLS for
zero-dependency simplicity.
Metrics: 0 dropped bytes (SHA-256 verified)
Stack: Python, bleak (BLE), asyncio, TCP sockets, SHA-256, GitHub Actions
Repository: https://github.com/Clarence6174

### TPS + Payment Gateway
Description: Distributed financial transaction processing system with async message
queuing, JWT-secured API gateway, and background result consumer.
Dataset: Synthetic transaction stream — 10k+ TPS load tested in staging.
Architecture: FastAPI + RabbitMQ + asyncpg + Redis. RabbitMQ chosen over Kafka for
lower operational overhead at target TPS. Redis for result caching and session state.
Stack: FastAPI, RabbitMQ, asyncpg, Redis, Docker Compose, AWS ECS Fargate, RDS, ECR
Status: Designed for horizontal scale on AWS

### Spotify Notifier
Description: Headless backend daemon for Spotify release monitoring. Zero browser
dependencies, zero GUI — pure server-side polling, delta detection, and SMTP dispatch.
Architecture: Spotipy + smtplib + cron. Deliberately dependency-minimal. No message
queue — release frequency makes simple polling sufficient at this scale.
Metrics: Less than 2 seconds end-to-end alert latency, 0 missed releases in testing.
Stack: Python, Spotipy, smtplib, cron, Linux systemd

## Published Work

### BLE-Assisted Peer Discovery for Low-Latency P2P Data Transfer in Constrained Edge Environments
Type: Technical article
Platform: Medium
URL: https://chinemeremmadu.medium.com/ble-assisted-peer-discovery-for-low-latency-p2p-data-transfer-in-constrained-edge-environments-9a761520811f
Summary: Formalises a hybrid BLE-discovery and TCP-streaming protocol for
resource-constrained edge devices, with SHA-256 integrity verification and
benchmarks against existing P2P approaches.

### On Building ML Pipelines That Don't Embarrass You at 3am
Type: Technical article (forthcoming)
Platform: Medium / arXiv
Summary: A field guide to production-grade ML infrastructure — what actually breaks,
why it breaks quietly, and the structural patterns that prevent 3am incidents.

### Anomaly Detection in Agricultural Time-Series Using Lightweight Transformer Encoders
Type: Research paper (forthcoming)
Platform: arXiv
Summary: Efficient transformer-based methods for detecting anomalies in sparse,
noisy IoT sensor streams from agricultural deployments with low-latency inference.

### The Case for Going Fully Headless in Backend ML Systems
Type: Technical article (forthcoming)
Platform: Medium
Summary: Why stripping browser dependencies and GUIs from ML backends leads to
leaner deployments, reproducible workflows, and fewer moving parts to debug.
